transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As you know, Line 6 is scheduled to produce 1,400 medical-device housings this week, but R-17 resin is temporarily unavailable. We have R-22, an alternate medical-grade resin, available for a controlled run. Before I issue the engineering authorization for this change, I need to hear from each of you on any constraints. Quality, process engineering, regulatory affairs, and production planning — please share any concerns or conditions you have so I can make a fully informed decision.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I checked the customer's revised control plan this morning, and it specifies that an alternate-resin run requires dimensional and tensile testing on exactly 50 first-off housings, with all 50 passing before the run can be released, plus retention of exactly 10 samples. I should also flag that the revised plan has not yet been attached to the change-control record.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: From my process trial, I found that R-22 must be dried at 80 degrees Celsius for exactly 4 hours and requires a 45-minute screw purge before molding. I recorded this in my engineering notebook but have not yet entered it into the production setup sheet, so it needs to be formally documented before we proceed.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a regulatory constraint. I confirmed with the resin manufacturer that the medical-grade declaration for R-22 applies only to supplier lot L2407-18. Our regulatory procedure requires lot-specific traceability and customer notification before any housings made from that lot can be shipped. I should also note that the supplier confirmation is currently only in my email and has not yet been placed in the release file, so it needs to be formally documented before we proceed.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share a capacity constraint from my updated capacity check. Friday's available Line 6 window is exactly 15.5 machine hours. After the required setup, the line can produce 100 housings per hour, which means the authorized run quantity must be exactly 1,400 housings rather than the full nominal order quantity. I have not yet posted the revised capacity sheet, so this needs to be formally documented as well.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Attach the revised control plan to the change-control record before production release.
Enter R-22 drying parameters (80°C, 4 hours) and 45-minute screw purge requirement into the production setup sheet before proceeding.
Place the supplier medical-grade confirmation for lot L2407-18 into the release file and ensure lot-specific traceability is recorded before shipment.
Complete customer notification before any housings made from lot L2407-18 are shipped.
Post the revised capacity sheet documenting the 15.5-hour Friday Line 6 window and the 1,400-housing authorized run quantity.
All 50 first-off housings must pass dimensional and tensile testing, and 10 samples must be retained before the run is released.
